title: The Dot-Com Bubble in 15 Seconds
learning_objective: The late-1990s internet boom inflated on investment far ahead of profit, and when it burst the speculation died but the technology did not.
style_notes: FIXTURE: derived from codex/examples/dotcom-bubble.lesson-script.example.json for page development. Narration is that example's, with slide-03 corrected against the research brief.
slide-03 said 'almost 400%'. The sourced figure is 600% (fact-02).
Archival late-1990s tech aesthetic shifting to modern in the final slide.
No dense text or tiny labels in generated images; the education lives in the voiceover.
FIXTURE (pending intro): the canonical 15-second format, which script-format.md says omits `intro`.

Reproduces what fal_media_agent.build_asset_manifest() actually emits: assets.talking_head_intro is ALWAYS written with provider 'pending' and a hardcoded path, even though the talking-head stage never ran and the mp4 does not exist.
Consequence: the manifest validates, but webpage-build.json's media_files_exist check is false on every standard run. The page must treat a declared-but-absent asset as a normal state, not an error.

slides.title: One of the biggest tech booms
slides.narration: The dot-com bubble was one of the biggest tech booms in history.
slides.visual_brief: Late-1990s stock market screen with tech stocks surging.

slides.title: Money before profits
slides.narration: Investors poured money into internet startups, often before they had profits, or even a viable business.
slides.visual_brief: Collage of early internet companies, websites, and startup offices.

slides.title: The Nasdaq climbs sixfold
slides.narration: From 1995 to 2000, the Nasdaq rose six hundred percent.
slides.visual_brief: Rising stock market graph alongside excited investors.

slides.title: Reality catches up
slides.narration: Then reality caught up. In 2000, the bubble burst, and tech stocks collapsed.
slides.visual_brief: Market chart suddenly turning sharply downward.

slides.title: Trillions wiped out
slides.narration: Thousands of companies disappeared, and five trillion dollars in market value were wiped out.
slides.visual_brief: Empty startup office with discarded computers.

slides.title: What survived
slides.narration: But the internet survived, and companies like Amazon emerged stronger.
slides.visual_brief: Modern tech company office transitioning from a 1990s computer.
